title: Chilling Final Cockpit Audio Emerges as Federal Agents Probe Florida Learjet Crash That Killed 9
snippet: Federal investigators are searching for answers after a Bahamas-bound private jet violently plunged into a South Florida neighborhood, killing all nine people aboard in a catastrophic fireball.
content:
A Bahamas-bound private jet carrying nine people plunged into a South Florida residential area on Sunday afternoon, leaving a massive crater and killing everyone on board in a terrifying crash captured on local dashcam footage.

The Learjet 60 had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas before crashing around 12:50 p.m. ET near Greenacres in Palm Beach County. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the incident a "horrific tragedy" as federal officials opened an immediate investigation into what caused the lethal dive.

Chilling Final Cockpit Transmissions

Air traffic control audio obtained from LiveATC captured the crew's increasingly desperate efforts to manage treacherous weather conditions moments before the crash. Initial chatter showed pilots attempting to navigate icing conditions and moderate turbulence while seeking permission to climb to a higher altitude for a safer ride.

Within less than a minute, the situation degraded into absolute catastrophe. Cockpit recordings captured distress calls reporting a sudden, extreme dive. Distress calls escalated as the aircraft dropped at 10,000 feet per minute, rapidly accelerating to over 20,000 feet per minute before Flightradar24 recorded a peak vertical descent exceeding 32,000 feet per minute.

"We're going to crash into the ground," a crew member declared in the cockpit recording as the plane began to bank wildly. The final words heard before impact were a harrowing declaration: "We're out of time."

Cataclysmic Ground Impact and Evacuations

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described the crash as "cataclysmic" during a press briefing, noting that eyewitnesses saw the plane come down "like a missile." Dashcam footage posted to social media showed the jet plummeting out of the sky before exploding into a massive fireball alongside a local roadway, narrowly missing passing motorists and nearby residences.

The crash created a massive crater near the entrance to a mobile home park and knocked out power to the surrounding neighborhood. Burning wreckage struck at least one nearby house, though state officials confirmed there were no immediate reports of ground injuries.

Local authorities temporarily evacuated approximately 600 residents to emergency shelters while hazmat units and first responders secured the extensive debris field.

NTSB Launches Formal Investigation

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) are currently leading the investigation. FAA records indicate the twin-engine business jet was registered to a Delaware corporation, though authorities have not yet released the identities of the victims.

While heavy rain, lightning, and a regional flood watch were present across Palm Beach County at the time of the flight, aviation experts suggest severe airframe icing combined with thunderstorm turbulence likely triggered an unrecoverable aerodynamic stall, leading to the rapid plunge.
